---
title: Package & publish
description: Turn a built app into a signed .mpk release and publish it to the Calimero app registry.
---

import { Steps, Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

A release of your app is a **`.mpk` package**: a gzip-compressed archive with your WASM, its ABI and a signed
`manifest.json` naming the package and version. Clusters install packages only from a registry, and every node that
runs one checks its signature and the digest of each WASM file before it runs.

<Steps>

1. **Create a signing key, once.** The key is your app's identity: a new version must be signed by the same key, or
   it is a different app.

   ```bash
   meroctl app signer new my-signing-key.json
   #   signerId: did:key:z6Mk...
   ```

   Keep the file secret and out of version control.

2. **Pack and sign** the release, from your app's crate:

   ```bash
   meroctl app pack . --key my-signing-key.json
   meroctl app inspect dist/com.example.my-app-1.0.0.mpk   # check it as a node does
   ```

   It builds the components, writes and signs `manifest.json`, and writes `dist/<package>-<version>.mpk`. The package
   id and display metadata (`name`, `description`, `icon`, ...) come from `[package.metadata.calimero]`, and the version
   from your crate's `version`. For every release after the first, pass `--previous <last .mpk>`: `pack` then warns
   about changes that break callers.

3. **Publish** it to the [Calimero app registry](https://apps.calimero.network) with an API key:

   ```bash
   export CALIMERO_REGISTRY_API_KEY=...
   meroctl app publish dist/com.example.my-app-1.0.0.mpk
   ```

   With `--org ORG`, the key is a Calimero Cloud organization's API key (scope `registry:publish`) instead.

   The registry checks the signature on upload, and that the package's `author` matches your registry account. You can
   also upload a `.mpk` from the Calimero Cloud console's Registry page.

</Steps>

<Aside type="caution">
`meroctl app pack` without `--key` signs with a well-known development key. That is fine for a local cluster, and the registry
refuses it: anyone holds that key, so it proves nothing.
</Aside>

## Private and public packages

A package belongs to the Cloud organization that publishes it and is **private** by default: only that
organization can deploy it. Making it **public** (`meroctl app publish --public`) lists it for everyone, after a
registry review.

## Next

[Deploy it on Calimero Cloud](/cloud/deploy/), then create an instance for each organization that uses it.

The manifest format and the exact checks a node runs on install are in the core reference's
[Packaging & signing](https://calimero-network.github.io/core/build/packaging-signing/).
